examples.question_text: Use tables of values to sketch $y=3^x$ and $y=\log_3x$ on the same axes. For the exponential graph, use $x=-2,-1,0,1,2$. Explain their reflection relationship, state each asymptote, and explain why the logarithmic graph is increasing and has no points with $x\le0$.

Sketch $y=\log_{\frac54}x$ and $y=\log_{\frac45}x$ on the same axes using $x=\frac{16}{25},\frac45,1,\frac54,\frac{25}{16}$. Use tables of values, state whether each curve is increasing or decreasing, and give their vertical asymptote.

methods.description: Compare the base with 1: bases greater than 1 give increasing curves; bases between 0 and 1 give decreasing curves.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Path/Logarithms_1 Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically.md lines 467–509, Investigation and Log Curve Transformations; the increasing condition is a>1, as stated at lines 54–55 and 485–490.

methods.description: Use equivalent index statements to find logarithmic outputs, plot the table points, and draw a smooth curve; repeat for each curve when comparing two graphs.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Path/Logarithms_1 Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically.md lines 431–454, Example: Graph logarithmic relationships using a table of values; lines 473–483, comparative sketching investigation.

methods.description: Use positive logarithmic inputs and the curve's approach to the y-axis to identify domain x>0 and vertical asymptote x=0; identify y=0 for the exponential partner.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Path/Logarithms_1 Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically.md lines 448–464, undefined inputs and asymptote questions.

methods.description: Compare an exponential graph with its logarithmic inverse by swapping table coordinates and reflecting in y=x.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Path/Logarithms_1 Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically.md lines 434–450, paired tables; lines 475–481 and 511–515, inverse reflection relationship.

exampleMappings.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Path/Logarithms_1 Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically.md lines 431–464, paired-graph worked example adapted from base 2 to base 3; lines 511–515, reflection in y=x.

booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Path/Logarithms_1 Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically.md lines 431–464, table-and-sketch method; lines 467–515, comparing logarithmic curves and base-dependent direction, adapted to bases 5/4 and 4/5.

coverage.summary: Authored two worked examples covering all four distinct assessed methods, including increasing and decreasing sketches and a same-axis comparison. Questions and solutions are separate; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Diagrams use editable TikZ, standard semantic colours, 10 pt labels and 8.5 pt ticks. No relation-led continuation rows require phantom gutters. Practice, quiz and theory content were neither altered nor re-audited. Independent example review and actual rendering verification remain for the coordinator's later stages.

examples.derivation: Independently calculated 3^x for x=-2,-1,0,1,2 as 1/9,1/3,1,3,9. Swapping coordinates gives logarithmic outputs -2,-1,0,1,2. The plotted expressions and marked points agree with both tables. The inverse graphs reflect in y=x; their asymptotes are respectively y=0 and x=0. Base 3>1 gives an increasing logarithmic curve, defined only for positive inputs. This adapts Book 1 lines 431–464 and 511–515 without introducing additional assessed methods.

Independently calculated (5/4)^n for n=-2,-1,0,1,2 as 16/25,4/5,1,5/4,25/16. These inputs give logarithmic outputs -2,-1,0,1,2 for base 5/4 and 2,1,0,-1,-2 for reciprocal base 4/5. Both plotted expressions and all marked coordinates agree. The first curve increases and the second decreases; both pass through (1,0), have positive inputs and vertical asymptote x=0. The table-and-sketch comparison follows Book 1 lines 431–515.

review.summary: All 25 exact assessment locators are mapped, and both examples cover the four distinct assessed methods, including increasing and decreasing sketches. No existing examples require dispositions, and no syllabus exception is needed. Questions and solutions are separate; editable prose and inline mathematics inherit solution blue. No relation-led working requires phantom gutters. Diagram definitions use the standard palette and specify 10 pt labels and 8.5 pt ticks. Final-size rendering verification remains with the coordinator. Accepted practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited.
